Smt. Ranjana Agnihotri - Public Prosecutor for responde

Heard on I.A. No.16194/2025, second application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to the present appellant.

2. This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 11.10.2023 passed in S.C. No.18/2023 by the learned Special Judge (POCSO Act, 2012) & 18 th Additional Sessions Judge, Jabalpur (M.P.),
whereby present appellant has been convicted under Sections 366 and 376(1) of IPC and sentenced to undergo five years R.I. with fine of Rs.1000/- and ten years R.I. with fine of Rs.2000/-
respectively, with default stipulations.

entities.text: Special Judge (POCSO Act, 2012) & 18 th Additional Sessions Judge, Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: All jail sentences are directed to be run concurrently.
3. It is submitted by learned counsel for present appellant that the present appellant, prosecutrix and their parents have settled the dispute between them and they have entered into a compromise.
The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the prosecutrix has no objection on the application for suspension of sentence filed on behalf of present appellant.
On merits, except the DNA report, there is no evidence on record.
The prosecutrix and their parents have not supported the story of prosecution and have turned hostile, therefore, no case is made out against the present appellant.
In view of the aforesaid, the present appellant deserves to be 2 CRA-16179-2023 given the benefit of suspension of sentence.
4 . Per contra, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the prosecutrix expresses his no objection over the application for suspension of sentence.

5. However, the learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the application on the ground that on 22.08.2024, the application for suspension of sentence on behalf of present appellant has been dismissed on merit.
Thereafter, except the period of one year, neither any changed circumstances is there nor any other ground is available for suspension of sentence.
Compromise between the parties also is no ground looking to the period of custody which is less than the half of the sentence awarded to the present appellant.

sentences.text: Having heard the learned counsels for the parties and after perusal of record, though as per the contentions of learned counsels for the parties, there is a compromise between the parties but the offences are not compoundable.
Moreover, the finding of learned trial Court of conviction and sentence is based on cogent and reliable evidence.
On this ground, the last application for suspension of sentence was dismissed vide order dated 22.08.2025.

As such, at this stage, keeping in view the attending facts and circumstances of the case, in the considered opinion of this Court,
this is not a fit case for granting the benefit of suspension of sentence to the present appellant.
7. Accordingly, I.A. No.16194/2025 is dismissed.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE ac/-
